sources.entry: pygame-ce - An actively developed drop-in replacement with new features and performance improvements (pygame fork).

summary.one_liner: pygame is a free, open-source, cross-platform Python library for building multimedia applications such as video games, built on SDL.
summary.what_it_does: Provides Python modules for 2D graphics (images, rectangles, polygons, animation), sound and music playback (WAV, MP3, OGG), and keyboard, mouse, and joystick input. Includes game-development helpers such as collision detection and sprite management. Uses the Simple DirectMedia Layer (SDL) library and several related libraries (SDL_ttf for fonts, SDL_mixer for audio, SDL_image for images) to abstract common tasks. The surfarray module optionally uses NumPy for multidimensional arrays. Bundled examples and a docs viewer (python -m pygame.docs) are included.
use_cases: write a 2D video game in Python
add sound effects and background music to a game
handle keyboard, mouse, or joystick controls
learn game programming with example programs
build multimedia or interactive desktop applications
notable: Cross-platform 2D game library with a long history and many bundled example games
Built-in offline documentation viewer via python -m pygame.docs
Can be built from source via setup.py for unreleased features
Free for closed-source and commercial games under LGPL 2.1, with examples in public domain
caveats: Source builds require compiling and installing dependencies manually; the README points to a wiki for details
Library is LGPL 2.1: modifications to pygame itself must be released under a compatible license
Online docs track the development version and may be newer than the pip release
